crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit in Investment Firms
children.blurb: An AI enablement audit in an investment firm maps where artificial intelligence and machine learning are used across the investment lifecycle, from research and portfolio construction to trading, operations, compliance and client reporting.

children.name: Fair Lending and Bias Testing
children.blurb: Fair lending and bias testing covers how lenders and credit decision systems evaluate applicants without unlawful disparate treatment or disparate impact on protected characteristics such as race, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance.

children.name: Explaining Models to Regulators and Clients
children.blurb: Explaining models to regulators and clients covers the practice of translating how a model works, what data it uses, and what its outputs mean into language that a non-specialist can act on.

children.name: Protecting Material Non-Public Information
children.blurb: Protecting material non-public information in AI-related firms covers the handling of confidential data about models, training runs, partnerships, regulatory findings, and financial results before public disclosure.

children.name: Verifying What a Model Produced
children.blurb: Verifying what a model produced covers the practices used to confirm that an AI system's outputs are accurate, consistent with their inputs, and fit for the purpose a firm assigns them.

sections.body: Governance and fiduciary risk is the work of making AI use accountable to the duties that investment firms and other fiduciaries already owe. In practice, teams run enablement audits before a model or tool goes into production, test lending and advice models for bias, and build explanations that satisfy regulators and clients. They also guard material non public information when staff use AI assistants, and they check model output before it enters a memo, a trade file, or a client report. This is not abstract ethics, it is controls, evidence, and sign off. The field sits where technology, compliance, and investment process meet.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, with fair lending testing using established statistical methods and model documentation becoming a normal expectation in regulated finance. Other parts remain hard. Explaining a large model to a regulator in a way that is faithful, stable, and useful is still an open problem, and bias testing can miss harms that appear only in combinations of features or in changing markets. Data loss prevention for AI tools is a moving target because prompts and outputs can leave a firm's boundary in ways that are difficult to reconstruct. Verification of AI output is often manual and uneven, and the site's tracking of 146 active AI lawsuits and 215 compliance and regulation pages shows how much of the field is still being defined through disputes and rulemaking. The honest limit is that no audit or test proves a model is safe or fair for all future conditions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here fit together as a control cycle rather than a list of separate topics. A reader who needs to know whether a firm is ready to use AI should start with The AI Enablement Audit in Investment Firms, which covers the review of people, data, and controls before deployment. Fair Lending and Bias Testing goes deeper into the statistical and legal side of testing credit and advice models for disparate impact. Explaining Models to Regulators and Clients addresses the documentation and communication work that turns a technical model into a defensible record. Protecting Material Non-Public Information covers the confidentiality controls around AI tools and prompts, and Verifying What a Model Produced covers the checks that keep generated or predicted output from being trusted without review. Together they show how governance and fiduciary risk is handled from pre deployment review through ongoing monitoring and evidence.
